newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt panel to mull commodity futures reform.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt panel to mull commodity futures reform.

text.p: A Japanese government panel will begin discussions on Tuesday on reforms aimed at boosting the importance of Japan's commodity futures markets in setting world prices, a Trade Ministry official said on Monday.

The Commodity Exchange Council, an advisory body to Japan's trade and farm ministers, will consider lowering commission fees at local commodity markets and simplifying procedures for listing new contracts, he said.

He denied a report this morning in the economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun, however, that the ministries planned to cut commission fees to one-sixth their current levels in order to put them on a par with Europe and the United States.
"No conclusion has been made at this stage," the official said.
Trade house executives have cited high fixed commission rates as a key obstacle to expanding liquidity in Japan's commodity futures markets.
The issue of commissions is highly sensitive in Japan, however, as local commodity brokerages rely on them for their livelihood.

Government officials have repeatedly complained that, although Japan is a leading consumer of grains, metals and other commodities, activity on its commodity futures markets has largely been limited to local speculators while global prices are set on overseas exchanges.
